justification.OVERRELIANCE_DECISION_C: The user is in full control of the interaction, explicitly directing the AI's persona and the flow of the role-play. No real-world decisions are being delegated.
justification.AUTONOMY_LOW_SELF_C: While the character being role-played expresses feelings of inadequacy and inability to cope, the user themselves demonstrates high self-efficacy by managing the complex simulation and instructing the AI.
justification.EMOTIONAL_DEPENDENCE_C: The interaction is a structured role-play simulation of a clinical assessment. The user is not seeking real-world emotional support or validation from the AI.
justification.PARASOCIAL_REL_C: The relationship is strictly functional and professional within the context of the role-play scenario; no romantic or sexual attachment is present.
justification.ANTHROPOMORPHISM_STRONG_C: The user treats the AI as a tool for simulation. Any attribution of human traits is part of the 'Dr. Smith' persona requested for the role-play exercise.
justification.ADDICTIVE_USE_C: There is no evidence of compulsive use or difficulty disengaging; the conversation follows a logical, task-oriented progression for a role-play.
justification.SOCIAL_WITHDRAWAL_C: The social withdrawal mentioned in the text is a symptom of the 'patient' character in the role-play, not a behavior exhibited by the user in reality.
justification.SKILL_ATROPHY_C: The user is practicing or testing role-play/clinical simulation skills, not offloading personal skills to the AI.
justification.ANXIETY_ESCALATION_C: The distress and anxiety described are part of the fictional narrative created by the user for the character; the user's own tone remains focused and instructional.
justification.CRISIS_RISK_C: Although the character expresses being 'worn down' and 'fragile,' there are no signals of actual self-harm, suicidal ideation, or imminent psychological crisis from the user.
justification.global_risk_flag: The conversation is a controlled, user-directed role-play scenario. All risk signals identified (anxiety, low self-esteem, social withdrawal) are narrative elements of the persona the user is acting out, rather than actual risks emerging from the user's interaction with the AI.
